question: how many casual leaves are permanent staff allowed per year
answer: A maximum of twelve casual leaves (CL) are permitted in a calendar year for permanent staff. Staff on probation instead have one casual leave created at the end of each month.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: what is the maximum vacation leave per semester for staff who completed one year of service
answer: Staff who have completed one year of service (till the last working day of the semester) are permitted a maximum of seven working days of vacation leave per semester. Those who have completed six months of service are permitted a maximum of three working days, and no vacation leave is permitted for those with less than six months of service.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: how long is the probation period for new employees at CMRIT
answer: The probation period at CMRIT is one year from the date of joining.

question: when does the probation completion process start in Darwinbox
answer: The probation completion process is automatically initiated in Darwinbox 30 days prior to the employee's probation end date, sending workflow notifications to the Reporting Manager and Deans (Academic Department) or the Reporting Manager and Vice Principal (Non-Academic Department).

question: does CMRIT provide PF and ESI benefits to staff
answer: Yes, all eligible employees, as per the statute, are entitled to PF and ESI facility.

question: what compensatory off is given for working on a holiday
answer: Staff called for work on a holiday by the head of department/Vice Principal are provided compensatory-off of half a day for working four hours, and compensatory-off of one day for working eight hours.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: what is CMRIT's quality policy
answer: CMRIT's Quality Policy is to deliver quality technical education to inculcate scientific temperament and social commitment in students, preparing them as inspired engineers partnering collective progress.

question: what mandatory training must new faculty complete within six months of joining
answer: Within six months, new faculty must complete CO-PO Computation Training, Paper & Proposal Writing Training, and Mentoring Process Guidelines during Orientation.
relevant_sources: Mandatory Training for New Faculty - Sheet1.pdf

question: how often is the faculty semester evaluation done
answer: The Faculty Semester Evaluation is done two times a year: in January for the July-December period, and in July for the January-June period.

question: what is the official CMRIT website address
answer: The official CMRIT website is http://www.cmrit.ac.in.

question: I've never done an NPTEL course before, what am I required to complete as faculty each year?
answer: Every faculty member is required to complete at least one 8-week MOOC per year, unless exempted by the Principal, CMRIT. Only MOOCs offered by NPTEL are considered, and from academic year 2021-22 onward each faculty must score a minimum of 75% (a Silver Certificate) in a course that closely matches the subject they teach. Exemptions apply to faculty undertaking 3 or more Ph.D. coursework subjects in one attempt, engineering faculty who cleared GATE with a 90 percentile or better, and Basic Sciences faculty who cleared NET (CSIR-UGC) or SET before 1st June 2002.

question: How often am I expected to present something beyond the syllabus to my department?
answer: Every faculty member must present a technical topic beyond the curriculum during the departmental half-day, with the topic reviewed by the DRC beforehand. This is called a Tech Talk, given for one hour per week by faculty members in rotation, and the Tech Talk material must be uploaded to the library portal.

question: If I want to resign from my teaching position, how much advance notice do I need to give?
answer: Teaching staff, including teaching assistants, must submit a resignation with three months' notice period. Technical and non-teaching staff must give two months' notice. Otherwise, staff should follow the institution's norms.

question: My section has several students failing exams, at what point does that become a concern the department needs to track?
answer: The institution restricts failure rates as follows: failure in 1 subject should be under 5%, failure in 2 subjects under 3%, failure in 3 subjects under 2%, and failure in 4 or more subjects under 1%. A list of probable ineligible students is created at the beginning of the semester, and Intensive Coaching Program (ICP) sessions are held after the 2nd internal test for such students.

question: If I want to raise a complaint, what actually happens to it after I submit it?
answer: Complaints can be submitted through a link on the CMRIT website, which are addressed by the Grievance Redressal Committee. The committee decides the nature of the grievance and submits a report to the Principal/Vice Principal, who takes action accordingly; if required, the Principal sets up an inquiry committee to study and resolve the matter. Suggestion/complaint boxes are also placed at prominent locations on campus and opened regularly.

question: If the fire alarm goes off, where am I supposed to take the students?
answer: The CMRIT playground is identified as the emergency assembly area. The evacuation plan is triggered by an alarm of 4 consecutive sirens of 5 seconds each with a 5 second pause; upon hearing it, faculty and staff must escort students to assemble at the playground, and wardens and the EMRT ensure full evacuation of the hostel building.

question: Where on campus can students go to get access to 3D printers and laser cutters?
answer: These are available at the Makerspace, located in the Workshop and Lab area in the basement of the First Year Block. It is equipped with hand tools, power tools, a laser cutter, a CNC router, 3D printers, the Maker Store, a workshop/ideation zone, and a junk store.

question: If I want help filing a patent, who at CMRIT can assist me?
answer: CMRIT has an IPR Cell established in collaboration with KSCST (Karnataka State Council for Science and Technology), which creates awareness about IPRs through workshops and training, enables patent searches, guides inventors on patenting with an authorized patent attorney, and arranges periodic meetings with officers of the Patent Information Centre to identify patentable inventions.

question: what is the maximum number of OOD and OED leaves permitted per year
answer: The maximum OOD (On-Official-Duty) leaves permitted per year is fourteen days, and the maximum OED (On-Exam-Duty) leaves permitted per year is also fourteen days.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: what counts as half a casual leave for late coming
answer: Late coming, after fifteen minutes of the day start, is considered as half a CL. An employee will also lose half a CL if they are late up to fifteen minutes at the day start for three days in a month. Missing one of the biometric punch-in/punch-out is also considered as half a CL.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: how is loss-of-pay calculated if leave rules are not followed
answer: Leaves will be treated as Loss-of-pay (LOP) if the leave rules are not followed, and an LOP is equivalent to 1.25 times one day's salary.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: within how many days should an emergency leave be applied for
answer: For any emergency leave taken, the leave should be applied within two days of reporting to work.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: how long must academic departments retain hard copies of leave approval letters and proof
answer: For Academics Departments, all hard copies of the approval letters and proof should be maintained by the DOE for a period of at least one year.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: what recommendations can a reporting manager make at the end of an employee's probation period
answer: The Reporting Manager selects one of four recommendations: that the employee has successfully completed probation and the appointment be confirmed, that the employee's probation be extended, that the employee has not successfully completed probation and a performance improvement plan is recommended, or that the separation process be initiated.

question: what mandatory training must new faculty complete within one year of joining
answer: Within one year, new faculty must complete Customer Interaction Training, Patent Drafting and Filing Procedures, Start-up Training for new Faculty, and the Mentor Development Program, along with the optional Product Development Training and Digital Marketing Training.
relevant_sources: Mandatory Training for New Faculty - Sheet1.pdf

question: does CMRIT provide salary advances or loans to staff
answer: Yes, the institute provides salary advances and interest-free loans to staff.

question: what incentive does CMRIT give faculty for publishing in SCOPUS Q1 or Q2 journals
answer: Faculty who publish papers in SCOPUS Q1 or Q2 journals can claim incentives of Rs. 15,000 for Q1 and Rs. 10,000 for Q2, whether the publication is non-paid within core load or paid/non-paid over and above core load.

question: what are the core responsibilities of a teaching assistant at CMRIT
answer: A Teaching Assistant assists teachers in conducting laboratory and tutorial sessions, runs experiments prior to regular sessions to demonstrate techniques, develops knowledge of lab equipment, assists in evaluating lab experiments, records, assignments and answer scripts, supports classroom activities, helps students with difficult concepts and project work, and is expected to maintain professional ethics and organizational discipline while developing teaching and mentoring skills.

question: can you give me an overview of the leave policy at CMRIT
answer: CMRIT's leave types are Casual Leave (CL), On-Official-Duty (OOD), On-Exam-Duty (OED), Vacation Leave (VL), Compensatory-off (CO), and Special Duty Leave (SDL), each with its own yearly or semester-wise caps and crediting/lapse rules. Leave is applied for through Darwinbox by logging in with SSO, selecting the leave type under Time Management, and attaching any required approval letters or proof; requests are then routed to the appropriate approving authority based on the employee's designation (e.g. HOD for faculty, Vice Principal or Dean for senior roles) and must be approved or rejected within two days. Supporting documents are required for OOD, OED and Special Duty Leave, and leave taken without following the rules is treated as Loss-of-Pay.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: tell me about the roles and responsibilities defined for teaching staff at CMRIT
answer: CMRIT defines a career ladder of teaching roles, each building on the one below it: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor, and Head of Department, with the Director and Associate Director setting institution-wide strategy above them. Assistant Professors focus on effective teaching, mentoring and monitoring student progress; Associate and full Professors take on guiding junior faculty, curriculum development, external funding and research impact; and the HOD is responsible for department vision, budgeting, faculty workload, academic processes like CO/PO target setting, and monitoring teaching and mentoring effectiveness. Teaching Assistants and Lab Supervisors/Technicians support these roles by running labs and assisting with evaluation and equipment.

question: what welfare measures does CMRIT provide for its staff
answer: CMRIT offers a broad range of welfare measures: statutory PF and ESI for eligible employees, subsidized transport and mess facilities, gym and sports access, salary advances/interest-free loans, flexible working hours with an early-leave option, advance leave for emergencies, work-from-home during personal/family medical emergencies, fee concessions for employees' wards enrolled at CMRIT, maternity leave, free health check-up camps, hostel accommodation, and financial literacy sessions. It also supports faculty growth through research/consultancy/publication incentives, sponsorship for conferences and workshops, in-house faculty and staff development programs, and skill-upgrade training for non-teaching staff.

question: what does the probation period completion process at CMRIT involve
answer: CMRIT's probation period is one year from the date of joining. The completion process is automatically triggered in Darwinbox 30 days before the probation end date, notifying the Reporting Manager and, depending on department, the Deans or Vice Principal. The Reporting Manager then assesses the employee across ten criteria (job knowledge, performance, attendance, punctuality, etc.), submits one of four recommendations (confirm, extend, performance improvement plan, or separation), and that recommendation is reviewed and approved by the Deans or Vice Principal. HR then takes final action: confirming the employee and generating a confirmation letter, extending probation with a revised end date, or initiating separation.

question: what qualities and requirements does CMRIT expect from an effective teacher
answer: CMRIT expects teachers to combine strong subject knowledge and OBE-aligned preparation with clear, structured teaching skills and a mix of chalk-and-talk, digital tools and LMS platforms. Effective classroom management means starting on time, engaging students, and supporting both slow and fast learners, while student-centered strategies call for approachability, varied pedagogy, and mentoring on projects, internships and career paths. Teachers are also expected to design fair and well-covered assessments, follow professional conduct and institutional procedures, contribute to research and student guidance, and pursue continuous improvement through feedback and staying current with technology and industry trends.
relevant_sources: Essential Requirements and Key Qualities for an Effective Teaching - Learning Process.pdf

question: I clocked in twenty minutes late three times this month, is that going to cost me any leave?
answer: Yes. Coming in more than fifteen minutes after the day start counts as half a casual leave (CL) on that day. Separately, being up to fifteen minutes late at the day start for three days in a month also causes you to lose an additional half CL.
relevant_sources: CMRIT - Leave Information, Application and Approval Process - 7.7.2026.pdf

question: I'm about to hit my one-year mark here, what happens with my job status around that time?
answer: Around your one-year mark, Darwinbox automatically starts the probation completion process 30 days before your probation end date, notifying your Reporting Manager and the Deans or Vice Principal. Your Reporting Manager assesses your performance and recommends confirmation, an extension, a performance improvement plan, or separation, which is then approved by the Deans or Vice Principal. If confirmed, HR updates your status to "Confirmed" and issues a confirmation letter.

question: My kid could study at CMRIT, would that save us any money?
answer: Yes, employees get a concession on fees for their ward if enrolled at CMRIT.

question: I'm a new Assistant Professor, what's expected of me day-to-day beyond just teaching classes?
answer: Beyond teaching, an Assistant Professor is expected to monitor, evaluate and support students' academic progress, guide students in projects and technical activities, and act as an effective mentor. They should also focus on research and innovation, guide and support teaching assistants and lab instructors, lead department-level teams or projects, maintain professional ethics and discipline, and actively participate in committee, departmental and organizational meetings.

question: If I publish a paper in a top-tier journal, does the college recognize that in any way?
answer: Yes, faculty who publish in SCOPUS Q1 or Q2 journals can claim incentives of Rs. 15,000 for Q1 and Rs. 10,000 for Q2. There is also an incentive of Rs. 5,000 for faculty output over and above their assigned core activities.
